title: Degenerate Matrix
statementMd:
The *determinant* of a matrix $2 × 2$ is defined as follows:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f36307f7f874a9b10893d1508d416e7c9a97fbb9.png)

A matrix is called *degenerate* if its determinant is equal to zero.

The *norm* $||*A*||$ of a matrix $*A*$ is defined as a maximum of absolute values of its elements.

You are given a matrix ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e78540a0de68f85833f82714a7141114b781276e.png). Consider any degenerate matrix $*B*$ such that norm $||*A* - *B*||$ is minimum possible. Determine $||*A* - *B*||$.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*a*$ and $*b*$ ($|*a*|, |*b*| ≤ 10^{9}$), the elements of the first row of matrix $*A*$.

The second line contains two integers $*c*$ and $*d*$ ($|*c*|, |*d*| ≤ 10^{9}$) the elements of the second row of matrix $*A*$.

## Output

Output a single real number, the minimum possible value of $||*A* - *B*||$. Your answer is considered to be correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed $10^{ - 9}$.

## Note

In the first sample matrix $*B*$ is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ce214ad27bde5d77f87492eedd74d34c745f72a1.png)

In the second sample matrix $*B*$ is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a07c34fbc6e9328bcb519d3f780eea6e02e5dc87.png)
